An optoelectronic semiconductor device is described that includes a semiconductor body (1). The semiconductor body (1) contains a semiconductor layer stack (2) made up of a p-doped semiconductor region (3), an n-doped semiconductor region (5), and an active layer (4) positioned between the p-doped semiconductor region (3) and the n-doped semiconductor region (5).

The device further includes a carrier (10) formed with a plastic material and provided with a first through-contact (11) and a second through-contact (12). A p-side contact layer (7) and an n-side contact layer (8) are also present, with at least portions of these contact layers located between the carrier (10) and the semiconductor body (1). The p-side contact layer (7) electrically couples the first through-contact (11) to the p-doped semiconductor region (3), while the n-side contact layer (8, 8A) electrically couples the second through-contact (12) to the n-doped semiconductor region (5).

In addition, an ESD protection element (15) is positioned between the carrier (10) and the semiconductor body (1). This ESD protection element (15) is electrically connected in a conductive manner to both the first through-contact (11) and the second through-contact (12), and its forward-bias direction is oriented opposite, in anti-parallel, to the forward direction of the semiconductor layer stack (2).
outputs.L3:
The component comprises a semiconductor body that includes a p-type semiconductor region, an n-type semiconductor region, and an active layer arranged between the p-type semiconductor region and the n-type semiconductor region. The active layer is configured to generate or receive electromagnetic radiation during operation of the component, depending on whether the component is used, for example, as a light-emitting or radiation-detecting device.

The semiconductor body is mounted on a support formed from a plastic material. The support includes a first via and a second via, which extend through the support and provide electrical connection paths from one side of the support to the semiconductor body. These vias serve as electrical feedthroughs for contacting the semiconductor regions of the component.

A p-contact layer electrically connects the first via to the p-type semiconductor region of the semiconductor body. In addition, an n-contact layer electrically connects the second via to the n-type semiconductor region. In this way, the p-type and n-type regions can be contacted separately through the respective vias in the plastic support.

The p-contact layer and the n-contact layer are arranged at least partially between the support and the semiconductor body. This configuration enables a compact structure in which the electrical contacts are integrated into the region between the support and the semiconductor body, thereby reducing the overall size of the component and improving mechanical and electrical integration.

Furthermore, an electrostatic discharge protection element is positioned between the support and the semiconductor body. The ESD protection element is electrically connected to both the first via and the second via. Its forward direction is oriented anti-parallel to the forward direction of the semiconductor layer sequence formed by the p-type region, the active layer, and the n-type region. As a result, the ESD protection element can protect the semiconductor body against electrostatic discharge events by providing a discharge path for voltage pulses of opposite polarity, thereby reducing the risk of damage to the active semiconductor structure.
outputs.L4:
An optoelectronic semiconductor component is provided which combines a semiconductor body with an electrically structured plastic support in a compact and mechanically stable arrangement. The semiconductor body comprises a semiconductor layer sequence having at least one active region suitable for generating or detecting electromagnetic radiation. The semiconductor layer sequence includes regions of different conductivity types, in particular a p-type semiconductor region and an n-type semiconductor region, which are electrically contacted by corresponding contact layers.

The semiconductor body is arranged on a plastic support. The plastic support may serve both as a mechanical carrier and as an electrical connection element for the component. For this purpose, the plastic support is provided with electrically conductive vias extending through the support. These vias allow electrical connection from an underside or mounting side of the component to the semiconductor body arranged on the opposite side of the support. In this way, the component can be mounted and contacted in a surface-mountable manner while maintaining a compact overall design.

Electrical connection between the vias of the plastic support and the semiconductor layer sequence is achieved by means of contact layers. A p-contact layer electrically connects one of the vias to the p-type region of the semiconductor layer sequence, while an n-contact layer electrically connects another via to the n-type region. The contact layers may be arranged between the semiconductor body and the plastic support and may be structured so that they are electrically insulated from one another. This configuration enables reliable current injection into, or current extraction from, the semiconductor layer sequence during operation of the component.

In addition to the semiconductor layer sequence, the component includes an electrostatic discharge protection element. This ESD protection element is arranged between the plastic support and the semiconductor body, so that it is integrated directly into the component rather than being provided as a separate external device. The ESD protection element is electrically connected to the semiconductor layer sequence in an anti-parallel manner. As a result, voltage spikes or discharge currents occurring in a reverse direction relative to the normal operating direction of the semiconductor layer sequence can be safely diverted through the ESD protection element.

The anti-parallel connection of the ESD protection element is particularly advantageous for sensitive optoelectronic components, such as light-emitting diodes, laser diodes, photodiodes, or radiation-emitting semiconductor chips, which may be damaged by electrostatic discharge during handling, assembly, or operation. By integrating the ESD protection element into the same component structure, the semiconductor layer sequence is protected without requiring additional space on an external circuit board. This improves the robustness of the component while preserving a small footprint.

The arrangement of the ESD protection element between the support and the semiconductor body also enables a particularly compact construction. Since the protection element is incorporated into the vertical build-up of the component, it does not substantially increase the lateral dimensions of the device. The vias in the plastic support and the p- and n-contact layers form an integrated electrical interconnection system, allowing both the optoelectronic semiconductor layer sequence and the ESD protection element to be contacted efficiently.

Overall, the component provides an optoelectronic semiconductor device in which electrical contacting, mechanical support, and electrostatic discharge protection are combined in a single integrated structure. The use of a plastic support with conductive vias allows simple external contacting, while the p- and n-contact layers ensure reliable connection to the corresponding semiconductor regions. The integrated anti-parallel ESD protection element protects the semiconductor layer sequence against damaging discharge events and contributes to a robust, compact, and cost-effective component design.
outputs.L5:
ESD, or Electrostatic Discharge, is the sudden flow of electricity between two objects with different electrical charges. Although it may seem harmless in everyday life, ESD can cause serious damage to sensitive electronic components, devices, and systems. Even a small discharge that a person cannot feel may be strong enough to weaken or destroy microchips, circuit boards, and other electronic parts.

ESD commonly occurs when people move across carpets, handle plastic materials, or work in dry environments where static electricity builds up easily. In electronics manufacturing, repair, and assembly, preventing ESD is essential to maintain product quality and reliability. Common ESD protection methods include using antistatic wrist straps, ESD-safe mats, grounding systems, conductive packaging, and controlled workstations.

Proper ESD control helps reduce failures, improve safety, and extend the lifespan of electronic products. Companies that handle electronic components often follow strict ESD standards and train employees to understand how static electricity works and how to prevent damage. By creating an ESD-safe environment, businesses can protect valuable equipment, reduce costs, and ensure consistent performance in electronic devices.

a carrier comprising an electrically insulating plastic material and having a first through-connection and a second through-connection extending through the carrier;

a semiconductor body disposed on the carrier, the semiconductor body comprising, in a stacking direction, a p-type semiconductor region, an active region, and an n-type semiconductor region;

In some embodiments, the electrostatic-discharge protection element is embedded at least partially in the carrier or arranged on a main surface of the carrier facing the semiconductor body.

In some embodiments, the electrostatic-discharge protection element comprises at least one of a diode, a Zener diode, a varistor, a transient-voltage-suppression element, or an ESD protection semiconductor structure.
